articles.headline: Knicks' Mike Brown criticizes free throw disparity in Game 3 loss
articles.description: Knicks coach Mike Brown criticized the officiating in Game 3 of the NBA Finals after the Spurs shot 24 free throws in the second half to New York's eight.

images.name: Mike Brown [600x400]
images.caption: After the Knicks saw their 13-game playoff winning streak come to a halt in Game 3 of the NBA Finals on Monday night, coach Mike Brown criticized the officiating, noting that the Spurs shot 24 free throws in the second half to New York's eight.

articles.headline: Wembanyama, Spurs stun Knicks at MSG to revive Finals hopes
articles.description: Victor Wembanyama had 32 points, eight rebounds and six assists in his first NBA Finals win Monday night as the Spurs returned to their "brand of basketball" to cut the Knicks' series lead to 2-1.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama  [600x400]
images.caption: Ahead of Monday's Game 3, Victor Wembanyama was seen unwinding at Gramercy Park, where he sketched a picture of the statue of Edwin Booth, the brother of John Wilkes Booth. Asked to evaluate his drawing, Wembanyama said, "Not bad, pretty good."

article.story: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Bennedict Mathurin scored 38 points in his home debut for Los Angeles and the Clippers held off the Denver Nuggets 115-114 on Thursday night. Denver’s Jamal Murray had a chance to tie it on three free throws with 0.9 seconds remaining after a foul from Derrick Jones Jr. Murray made the first two before missing the third, with time expiring on the rebound. Kawhi Leonard added 23 points, and Jones had 22 to help the Clippers improve to 21-7 since Dec. 20. Both teams were coming off the All-Star break. Mathurin, acquired from Indiana at the trade deadline, was 12 of 22 from the field, while Leonard went 8 of 18 and scored at least 20 points for the 34th consecutive game. Nikloa Jokic had 22 points and 17 rebounds for Denver. Murray scored 20 points, Bruce Brown had 19, and Cam Johnson and Julian Strawther added 18 each. Denver was without Aaron Gordon (hamstring) for the 10th consecutive game, while Peyton Watson (hamstring) has missed the past four. Tempers flared with 10:27 remaining when the Clippers’ Yanic Konan Niederhauser, Kris Dunn and Mathurin tangled with the Nuggets’ Jonas Valanciunas under the Denver basket following a free throw. Dunn, Mathurin and Valanciunas all received technical fouls, with Denver making one technical free throw for an 83-83 tie. The Nuggets tied in 107-107 with 46 seconds remaining on a shot inside from Jokic. The Clippers went up 115-112 with nine seconds left on two free throws from Mathurin. Up next Nuggets: At Portland on Friday night. Clippers: At Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night. ------ AP NBA: https://apnews.com/hub/nba
